title: Atlas queue migration
body: Atlas queue migration moves every background job off the legacy RabbitMQ cluster onto a new queue. It is owned by Ana Reyes on the Platform team.

title: Ledger billing pipeline
body: Ledger billing pipeline rebuilds the nightly billing export as a streaming pipeline. It is owned by Lena Novak on the Data team.

title: Beacon mobile push
body: Beacon mobile push rebuilds push notifications for the iOS and Android apps. It is owned by Hana Sato on the Mobile team.

title: Cobalt payment retries
body: Cobalt payment retries retries failed card payments without double-charging. It is owned by Dev Patel on the Payments team.

title: Sentinel access reviews
body: Sentinel access reviews automates periodic reviews of who can access production. It is owned by Jade Wong on the Security team.

title: Harbor container platform
body: Harbor container platform moves services from virtual machines to containers. It is owned by Ana Reyes on the Platform team.

title: Prism analytics warehouse
body: Prism analytics warehouse consolidates analytics into one warehouse with self-serve dashboards. It is owned by Lena Novak on the Data team.

title: Quill offline notes
body: Quill offline notes lets field staff take notes offline and sync later. It is owned by Hana Sato on the Mobile team.

title: Vault key rotation
body: Vault key rotation rotates every encryption key on a fixed schedule. It is owned by Jade Wong on the Security team.

title: Relay webhook service
body: Relay webhook service delivers payment events to customers' webhooks. It is owned by Dev Patel on the Payments team.

title: Atlas queue migration: target queue is Amazon SQS
body: For Atlas queue migration, we decided the target queue is Amazon SQS, because the team already runs on AWS.

title: Atlas queue migration: target queue is NATS JetStream
body: We replaced the earlier decision (Amazon SQS). For Atlas queue migration, the target queue is now NATS JetStream, because SQS could not meet our message-ordering needs in load tests.

title: Ledger billing pipeline: storage engine is Amazon Redshift
body: For Ledger billing pipeline, we decided the storage engine is Amazon Redshift, because it was the default warehouse.

title: Ledger billing pipeline: storage engine is Google BigQuery
body: We replaced the earlier decision (Amazon Redshift). For Ledger billing pipeline, the storage engine is now Google BigQuery, because Redshift costs grew faster than usage.

title: Ledger billing pipeline: storage engine is ClickHouse
body: We replaced the earlier decision (Google BigQuery). For Ledger billing pipeline, the storage engine is now ClickHouse, because BigQuery query costs were unpredictable for nightly backfills.

title: Beacon mobile push: push provider is OneSignal
body: For Beacon mobile push, we decided the push provider is OneSignal, because it was fastest to integrate.

title: Beacon mobile push: push provider is Firebase Cloud Messaging
body: We replaced the earlier decision (OneSignal). For Beacon mobile push, the push provider is now Firebase Cloud Messaging, because OneSignal pricing changed and we need delivery receipts.

title: Cobalt payment retries: retry policy is three fixed retries one hour apart
body: For Cobalt payment retries, we decided the retry policy is three fixed retries one hour apart, because it matched the old behaviour.

fields.choice: three fixed retries one hour apart

title: Cobalt payment retries: retry policy is exponential backoff with jitter
body: We replaced the earlier decision (three fixed retries one hour apart). For Cobalt payment retries, the retry policy is now exponential backoff with jitter, because fixed retries caused bursts against the card network.

title: Sentinel access reviews: review cadence is quarterly reviews
body: For Sentinel access reviews, we decided the review cadence is quarterly reviews, because auditors asked for quarterly evidence.

title: Sentinel access reviews: review cadence is monthly reviews
body: We replaced the earlier decision (quarterly reviews). For Sentinel access reviews, the review cadence is now monthly reviews, because quarterly reviews missed leavers for too long.

title: Harbor container platform: orchestrator is HashiCorp Nomad
body: For Harbor container platform, we decided the orchestrator is HashiCorp Nomad, because it is simpler to operate.

title: Harbor container platform: orchestrator is Kubernetes on EKS
body: We replaced the earlier decision (HashiCorp Nomad). For Harbor container platform, the orchestrator is now Kubernetes on EKS, because every vendor tool we need assumes Kubernetes.

title: Prism analytics warehouse: dashboard tool is Looker
body: For Prism analytics warehouse, we decided the dashboard tool is Looker, because the data team knew it already.

title: Prism analytics warehouse: dashboard tool is Metabase
body: We replaced the earlier decision (Looker). For Prism analytics warehouse, the dashboard tool is now Metabase, because Looker seat costs blocked self-serve access.

title: Vault key rotation: rotation interval is every 180 days
body: For Vault key rotation, we decided the rotation interval is every 180 days, because it matched the compliance minimum.

title: Vault key rotation: rotation interval is every 90 days
body: We replaced the earlier decision (every 180 days). For Vault key rotation, the rotation interval is now every 90 days, because a customer contract required 90 days.

title: Vault key rotation: rotation interval is every 30 days
body: We replaced the earlier decision (every 90 days). For Vault key rotation, the rotation interval is now every 30 days, because the security review asked for shorter key lifetimes.

title: Relay webhook service: delivery guarantee is at-most-once delivery
body: For Relay webhook service, we decided the delivery guarantee is at-most-once delivery, because it kept the first version simple.

title: Relay webhook service: delivery guarantee is at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys
body: We replaced the earlier decision (at-most-once delivery). For Relay webhook service, the delivery guarantee is now at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys, because customers lost events during deploys.
